options.metric: Annual number of motorist deaths and cyclist deaths
options.reason: Absolute counts directly answer how many motorist and cyclist deaths were reported in each year.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in all 13 years; the counts ranged from 72–139 motorist deaths and 10–31 cyclist deaths, and were 81 versus 23 in 2025.
options.interpretation: The grouped bars answer the year-by-year comparison in absolute numbers: motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year, including 81 versus 23 in 2025. This is a defensible framing because the question asks how the annual death counts compare, while retaining the size of the difference. It does not express the cyclist count relative to the motorist count or adjust deaths for exposure, population, or crash volume. No in-period rows are omitted for NULL death counts (0 of 2,132,218, 0.00%); all rows outside 2013–2025 are excluded (2012: 100,545 rows (4.43% of file); 2026: 36,424 rows (1.61% of file)), and no included year is partial.

options.metric: Cyclist deaths as a percentage of motorist deaths
options.reason: A ratio makes the relative scale of cyclist deaths against motorist deaths easy to compare across years.
options.answer: Cyclist deaths peaked relative to motorist deaths in 2019 at 37.8% (31 versus 82), and were 28.4% (23 versus 81) in 2025.
options.interpretation: The line shows the year-by-year relative comparison: cyclist deaths were highest against motorist deaths in 2019 at 37.8%, and stood at 28.4% in 2025. This ratio is defensible because it compares cyclist deaths with the motorist-death count within each year, making the relative gap visible over time. It leaves the absolute number of deaths less prominent, so a similar ratio can represent different annual totals. No in-period rows are omitted for NULL death counts (0 of 2,132,218, 0.00%); all rows outside 2013–2025 are excluded (2012: 100,545 rows (4.43% of file); 2026: 36,424 rows (1.61% of file)), and no included year is partial.
